edges.description: The substitution replaces a buried isoleucine with a hydrophilic threonine inside the AAA+ motor domain, so the primary consequence is on the fold of the ATPase itself rather than on its expression level.

A partly non-functional motor subunit lowers, but does not abolish, the proteolytic throughput of the 26S proteasome. The in vivo rescue assay is what fixes the direction and the magnitude: human wild-type PSMC1 nearly fully rescued an Rpt2-depletion phenotype while the mutant rescued it only partly.
Substrates tagged for degradation are not cleared, so polyubiquitinated protein accumulates in an insoluble fraction.
Neurons are the cell type least able to tolerate a fall in degradative capacity, having no route to dilute an undegraded burden by division.

Eye-specific RNAi depletes the fly orthologue of PSMC1, creating the loss of 26S function that the human allele is proposed to cause partially. The rescue arm then reads out how much function the patient allele retains.
edges.limitations: The perturbation is RNAi knockdown of the orthologue, not the missense allele in its native locus, and the readout tissue is the compound eye rather than neurons. Ommatidial fusion and depigmentation have no human counterpart, so the assay reports residual protein function and not the disease phenotype. Rescue was scored morphologically; no proteasome activity or ubiquitin-conjugate measurement was made in the rescued flies.
edges.source: Drosophila Rpt2 eye knockdown with human PSMC1 rescue

edges.description: Removing Psmc1 from neurons depletes the 26S proteasome while leaving the 20S core intact, and is sufficient on its own to cause inclusion pathology and neurodegeneration - which is the claim this node makes about neuronal dependence on 26S function.
edges.limitations: Genotype mismatch in both direction and timing: a complete conditional null in defined postnatal neuronal populations, against a germline hypomorphic missense present in every cell from conception. The output is adult-onset neurodegeneration with Lewy-like inclusions - a Parkinson-disease phenotype - whereas the human disease is a static, congenital neurodevelopmental one with no reported neurodegeneration or parkinsonism. Nothing in the model addresses hearing, growth, genital development or the liver findings. It supports the neuronal-dependence step only.

nodes.description: Rpt2/PSMC1 is one of the six AAA+ ATPases that form the base ring of the 19S regulatory particle and provide the mechanical work of substrate engagement, unfolding and translocation into the 20S core. p.I328 lies within the hydrophobic core of the motor domain, so replacing it is expected to perturb the folded structure of the ring subunit. No biochemical measurement of ATPase activity in patient material has been reported, so this node is supported by structural prediction plus the in vivo rescue result, not by a direct assay.

nodes.description: A neuron-restricted conditional null generated to model Parkinson disease, not this syndrome. It is curated here because it is the only in vivo demonstration that neurons specifically require the 26S proteasome, and because the germline null is embryonic lethal, so it is the only mammalian route to the question.

Reduced ubiquitin-dependent degradation through the 26S holoenzyme. This is the shared node of the neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies: lesions in the 20S core (PSMB1), the 19S lid (PSMD12) and the 19S base (PSMC1, PSMC3) all converge here. The deficit in this disease is partial - a complete loss of the orthologue is lethal in mice and in worms - which is why a viable human phenotype exists at all.
